subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 48-year-old man with obesity and biopsy-proven hepatic steatosis participates in a study of hepatic lipogenesis after a high-carbohydrate meal. Isotope labeling shows that the newly synthesized fatty acids released by his liver are almost entirely 16-carbon saturated chains.
question: Which of the following is the predominant direct product of the fatty acid synthase complex in these hepatocytes?
explanation_correct: The cytosolic fatty acid synthase complex uses acetyl-CoA as a primer and malonyl-CoA as the two-carbon donor, adding units in NADPH-dependent cycles until the chain reaches 16 carbons. The direct product is palmitate (16:0); longer and unsaturated fatty acids are made afterward by elongases and desaturases in the endoplasmic reticulum.

explanation_incorrect.A: Stearate (18:0) is produced by elongation of palmitate in the endoplasmic reticulum, not by fatty acid synthase.
explanation_incorrect.B: Oleate (18:1) is produced by delta-9 desaturation of stearate in the endoplasmic reticulum.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acetyl-CoA is the primer that initiates synthesis, not the product of the complex.
explanation_incorrect.D: Malonyl-CoA is the substrate added during each cycle and is decarboxylated as the two-carbon unit is incorporated.

educationalObjective: Fatty acid synthase produces palmitate (16:0) from acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA using NADPH.
